page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading) running at 2.5 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory density is exceptionally high, supplying 256.0 GB of RAM at a 1:16 core-to-memory ratio (16.0 GB per vCPU). Local high-speed storage is integrated directly via a 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No hardware GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark data demonstrates typical Graviton2 performance characteristics, excelling in multi-threaded operational density while displaying lower single-core throughput. The instance recorded 24,289.25 in stress-ng multi-core testing and an average Geekbench multi-core score of 8,543.0, contrasted by weaker single-threaded results such as 962.0 on Geekbench single-core and 20.32 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. In-memory data structures perform reliably, with Redis SET benchmarks achieving 18.95 million operations per second and database operation scores landing in the middle 50% percentile (10,266.45 on PassMark). Large uncached memory reads achieve 155.82 GB/sec, while cached 16 KB read throughput tops 947.22 GB/sec.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the x2gd.4xlarge prioritizes memory allocation per core, offering strong cost-to-capacity metrics for memory-bound systems compared to standard x86 memory-heavy instances. However, workloads requiring intensive vector calculations or specialized cryptographic acceleration face limitations, as the Graviton2 processor lacks AVX/AMX instruction sets and registers lower PassMark encryption scores (2,185.54). Similarly, LLM inference tests show constrained capabilities, yielding poor prompt processing speeds for 7B models at 16.12 tokens per second.

The x2gd.4xlarge is designed primarily for memory-intensive workloads that require large RAM footprints without high per-thread compute demands. Typical deployments include in-memory caches like Redis and Memcached, large relational and NoSQL databases, real-time analytics engines, and high-memory batch processing where local scratch storage benefits from the bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 Graviton2 architecture running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It offers 16 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.5 GHz and 256.0 GB of memory, yielding an extensive 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage includes a 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero GPUs present. Benchmarks show solid multi-core throughput (Geekbench multi-core of 8,543.0) and high memory operations (18.95 million Redis SET ops/sec), though single-threaded performance and instruction-heavy tasks are comparatively restrained. The instance provides strong resource density and cost efficiency for memory-dominated workloads such as in-memory caching systems, distributed data stores, relational databases, and real-time big data pipelines needing large RAM footprints and local temporary NVMe storage.
